title: Spring warmth gave no clear repeated narrowing of frog detection seasons in eight US samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested whether warm springs narrow seasonal frog detection curves after adjustment for peak date and detection level. We used American toad and gray treefrog records from Northeast and Midwest US NAAMP routes in 2001-2008 and 2009-2015. A quadratic logit model used route-observer effects, real survey dates and night weather. Seven of eight warmth by curvature estimates were positive, which means broader fitted curves. All eight year-bootstrap intervals adjusted for eight tests included zero. Ten-stop runs kept all signs. Added year effects and removal of 2012 gave no repeated narrowing. A raw rebuild matched the reused public panels. This is a new test on shared observations, not independent validation of earlier timing results. Sparse visits, a quadratic shape, selected routes, few years and model bias limit inference. Detection width is not biological season length. Air pollution was not tested. Code, provenance, derived panels, checks, tables and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Warmth by curvature estimates. Thin lines show 95% year-bootstrap intervals. Thick lines show nominal 99.375% intervals for eight tests. Negative values mean stronger downward curvature. All adjusted intervals include zero.
